I was in the process of verifying a French grammar multiple choice question about the correct verb tense to use with "dès que" in a future context.

The question asks to fill in: "Dès que vous ___ ce gâteau, vous comprendrez pourquoi il est fameux."

The marked correct answer is "aurez goûté" (futur antérieur), which is indeed the correct choice because:
- "Dès que" with a main clause in futur simple ("comprendrez") requires the subordinate clause to use futur antérieur when the subordinate action will be completed before the main action
- "aurez goûté" (will have tasted) correctly shows this temporal relationship
- The other options (goûtez, goûterez, goûteriez) do not follow this grammar rule
